content.title: Recommendations for the regimen and duration of anticoagulation after pulmonary embolism in patients without cancer (section 8.4)
content.summary: Guidance on extended anticoagulation after pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients without cancer, with trial evidence comparing VKAs, NOACs (eg, rivaroxaban), aspirin, and sulodexide; specific caution for patients with antiphospholipid syndrome (especially triple-positive).
key_points: In high-risk patients with antiphospholipid syndrome (testing triple-positive for lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, and anti-β2-glycoprotein I), rivaroxaban was associated with an increased rate of thromboembolic and major bleeding events compared with warfarin; at present NOACs are not an alternative to VKAs for these patients.
Two trials (total n ≈ 1224) found that extended therapy with aspirin after termination of standard oral anticoagulation was associated with ~30–35% reduction in recurrence compared with placebo.
Another trial demonstrated superiority of anticoagulation with rivaroxaban (20 or 10 mg once daily) over aspirin for secondary prophylaxis of VTE recurrence.

A randomized, placebo-controlled study of sulodexide in 615 patients with a first VTE event (after 3–12 months of oral anticoagulant treatment) reduced recurrence by approximately 45% with no apparent increase in bleeding; only ~8% of patients in that study had PE as the index event.

trial_details.outcome: Increased rate of thromboembolic and major bleeding events with rivaroxaban; composite primary outcome HR ~6.7 (95% CI quoted in text).
trial_details.implication: NOACs not an alternative to VKAs in these patients.

trial_details.population: Patients eligible for extended therapy after standard anticoagulation
Patients requiring secondary prophylaxis of VTE recurrence
trial_details.outcome: Rivaroxaban superior to aspirin for secondary prophylaxis (reference to trial showing superiority).

trial_details.population: Patients with first VTE event without identifiable risk factor who completed 3–12 months anticoagulation
trial_details.outcome: Reduced risk of recurrence by ~45% with no apparent bleeding increase; only ~8% had PE as index event.

recommendations_summary: Therapeutic anticoagulation for ≥3 months is recommended for all patients with PE.
Discontinuation of anticoagulation after 3 months is recommended for patients with transient/reversible major risk factors.
Extension of anticoagulation beyond 3 months is recommended for patients with recurrent VTE or persistent risk factors; decisions individualized based on risk/benefit.

For extended oral anticoagulation in patients without cancer, a reduced NOAC dose (eg, apixaban 2.5 mg b.i.d. or rivaroxaban 10 mg o.d.) may be considered after 6 months of therapeutic anticoagulation for some patients.
If patients refuse or cannot tolerate anticoagulants, aspirin or sulodexide may be considered for extended VTE prophylaxis.
practical_notes: Take into account antiphospholipid antibody status (especially triple-positive) when choosing anticoagulant regimen.
Follow-up of patients on extended anticoagulation should reassess drug tolerance, adherence, hepatic and renal function, and bleeding risk at regular intervals.
content.figure: A recommendations table/figure is present summarizing classes and levels of evidence for different scenarios (discontinuation after 3 months, extension beyond 3 months, NOAC dosing in extended therapy, alternatives such as aspirin/sulodexide).
